programme: A lymphocyte-lineage/terminal-differentiation checkpoint built from PRDM1 (BLIMP1), which directly targets TBX21, CIITA and PAX5 in this network; RFXAP, the RFX-complex partner of CIITA that drives MHC class II gene transcription (HLA-DR/DP/DQ/DM/DO, HLA-E); TBX21 (T-bet), which commits CD4+/CD8+ T cells to a Th1/cytotoxic effector program (IFNG, IL2, CXCR3, STAT4, JAK3, HAVCR2); EBF1, the B-lineage commitment factor (PAX5, CD19, CD79A, VPREB1, IGLL1, BCR); and IKZF1 (Ikaros), a pan-lymphoid factor upstream of both branches (CD3D, CD4, GATA3, STAT1, IKZF3). Together these five recapitulate the classic PRDM1-centered switch that represses CIITA-driven MHC-II and PAX5-driven B-cell identity while inducing TBX21-driven Th1 effector fate, i.e. the module a bulk tumor transcriptome shows when it contains an organized lymphocytic infiltrate.
role_in_a: In colorectal cancer this is the tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte axis underlying the well-described MSI-high/dMMR immune-hot phenotype: dense CD4/CD8 infiltration coupled to tumor or stromal HLA class II expression, with PRDM1 note as coordinating both antigen-presentation and Th1 effector output. PMID 25445815 documents exactly this link in CRC — HLA class II regulatory gene mutation associated with high CD4+ T cell infiltration — and PMID 42396452 places PRDM1 at a described 'hub in immune differentiation' in CRC.
role_in_b: In papillary RCC no PMID in this record places any of the five factors mechanistically, but Open Targets independently scores EBF1 (86th pct), PRDM1 (81st pct) and IKZF1 (91st pct) of ~2369 genes against this disease, consistent with genetic/genomic evidence that a lymphoid infiltration programme is active in at least some papillary RCC tumors, in line with the disease's known but variable immune-cell content.
shared_axis: Both are epithelial solid tumors profiled in bulk, so their expression networks pick up whichever admixed lymphocytic infiltrate is present; where an infiltrate exists, it is organized by the same PRDM1/RFXAP/TBX21/EBF1/IKZF1 lymphocyte-differentiation hierarchy regardless of whether the epithelium of origin is colorectal or renal, which is why the same factor set recurs across a large share of patient groups in both diseases without needing any epithelial cross-talk between the two cancers.
reasoning: The module is clearly nameable from canonical B/T lymphocyte regulon biology (PRDM1 target list alone contains TBX21, CIITA and PAX5), and CRC placement is solid (RFXAP-CD4 infiltration paper is a direct hit). But KIRP placement rests only on Open Targets percentile scores, not on any retrieved mechanistic paper, and two of the CRC PMIDs (EBF1-fibroblast, TBX21-metastasis) document non-lymphocyte mechanisms for those same factors in CRC — so the CRC-KIRP connection through this specific programme is argued, not shown directly for the pair.
support: 25445815 — CD4+ T cell infiltration in CRC correlates with mutation of HLA class II regulatory genes, directly supporting the RFXAP/CIITA-MHCII arm in CRC; 42396452 — describes PRDM1 as a hub of immune differentiation with a stated role in CRC progression; 42230505 — colon adenocarcinoma cell-derived galectins modulate CD4+ T cell differentiation, indirect context for the TBX21/Th1 arm in CRC; 39744435 — places TBX21 in CRC but via a tumor-intrinsic ARHGAP29/MYCT1/GSK3β metastasis-suppressor mechanism, not the Th1 target program used here; 39002521 — places EBF1 in CRC but via an EBF1-COX4I2 cancer-associated-fibroblast axis, not the B-lineage mechanism used here; 42228147 and 41603279 — place IKZF1 (with BCAT1) in CRC/rectal cancer as a circulating-tumor-DNA methylation biomarker, not a mechanistic lymphocyte role.
how_to_falsify: Deconvolve or sort CD4+/CD8+ T cells and B cells from matched CRC and papillary RCC tumors and test whether PRDM1 induction tracks with TBX21 upregulation and RFXAP/CIITA-target (HLA-DR/DP/DQ) repression the same way in both tumor types; if papillary RCC TILs show PRDM1 activity uncoupled from TBX21 induction or from HLA-II repression (or if EBF1/PAX5+ B cells are essentially absent from papillary RCC infiltrates), the shared-programme account fails even though infiltration itself is present.
caveats: Tissue pairing is colorectal epithelium vs papillary renal epithelium — the module is a lymphocyte-lineage programme, not epithelial biology, so the signal is best read as coming from admixed immune infiltrate in bulk expression, in both diseases. Support is drawn from 266 patient-group comparisons across only 2 independent cohort pairs, and the carrying factors' recurrence (88-112/266, roughly 33-42%) is well below near-unanimous; this is a recurring signal, not a dominant one. KIRP support rests entirely on Open Targets aggregate percentile scores for 3 of 5 factors (EBF1, PRDM1, IKZF1) — no PMID here documents any of the five factors mechanistically in papillary RCC, and TBX21/RFXAP show no Open Targets association in KIRP at all. The remaining eight factors in the full list (HCFC1, ID2, MAFB, HOXC8, CEBPE, POU3F1, ZNF331, and the highest-recurrence factor HCFC1 itself) sit outside this module — cell-cycle, macrophage/podocyte, BMP, granulocyte, neural and methylation-biomarker programs respectively — and are not explained by this account. No tissue-generic master regulator of colon or kidney epithelium was reached for, and the excluded single-view factors add no additional lymphocyte-lineage members that would change this story.
